rejected.title: Shades of meaning
card: Near synonyms are words with similar meanings. They are not identical. Each one carries a slightly different shade of meaning.
Take ask, request, demand and plead. Ask is neutral. Request is polite and formal. Demand is forceful and expects a yes. Plead is emotional and desperate.
Many words also carry a feeling beyond their plain meaning. Slim and skinny both mean thin, but slim sounds positive and skinny can sound negative.
To choose the best word, ask what the writer wants the reader to feel or picture. Then pick the word whose shade fits that purpose most closely.
rejected.remember: Near synonyms differ in force and feeling, so the precise word gives the exact meaning.

a.q: A writer changes 'Sam asked for a refund' to 'Sam demanded a refund'. How does this change the way Sam comes across?
opts: Sam now sounds forceful and expects a yes
Sam now sounds polite and formal
Sam now sounds emotional and desperate
Sam sounds the same, as the words are synonyms
a.why: Demand is forceful and expects a yes, so Sam seems firm and insistent. Desperate is tempting because demand is a strong word, but that is the shade of plead. Near synonyms are not identical, so swapping one for another does change the meaning.
a.clue: Which shade does demand carry that ask does not?

b.q: Jess is writing a story. She wants to show that her character, Mia, is upset and desperate when she speaks to her boss. Which sentence fits best?
opts: Mia pleaded with her boss to keep her job
Mia asked her boss to let her keep her job
Mia demanded that her boss let her keep her job
Mia requested that her boss let her keep her job
b.why: Pleaded carries emotion and desperation, which matches what Jess wants to show. Demanded is tempting because it is strong, but it sounds forceful and expects a yes, not desperate. Asked is neutral and requested is polite and formal.
b.clue: Which word carries emotion and desperation, not force?

a.q: Why does a writer choose one near synonym over another, such as plead instead of ask?
opts: Each word carries a different shade of meaning
Longer words always sound more convincing
Synonyms are never allowed to be repeated
Plain words have no effect on a reader
a.why: Near synonyms are close but not identical, so each one shapes the meaning a little differently. Choosing plead over ask adds desperation. Length does not decide the effect: a short word can be just as precise.
a.clue: Think about what each word adds beyond its plain meaning.

b.q: Jess wants to show that her character is upset and desperate when she speaks to her boss. Which sentence uses the most precise word?
opts: Jess pleaded with her boss to keep her job
Jess asked her boss to keep her job
Jess demanded that her boss keep her job
Jess requested that her boss keep her job
b.why: Pleaded shows desperation and strong emotion, which matches the purpose. Demanded is tempting because it is strong, but it sounds forceful and expects a yes, not desperate. Asked and requested are too calm or formal.
b.clue: Which word carries emotion and desperation, not force?

a.best: Each word carries a different shade of meaning

b.best: Jess pleaded with her boss to keep her job

problems.detail: The stem says Jess is the writer ('her character'), but every option makes Jess the one speaking to the boss. Students may wonder whether Jess is the writer or the character. Name the character differently, e.g. 'Jess wants to show that her character, Mia, is upset...'.

The three wrong options all use absolutes ('no effect', 'never', 'always'). The right option is the only one without one, and it repeats the title's phrase 'shade of meaning', so a student could pick it without knowing the idea.
